source_text:
Τούτῳ τοιγαροῦν καὶ ἡμεῖς τῷ ἔθει δουλεύοντες, καὶ νόμον ἡγούμενοι κάλλιστον πᾶν τὸ τοῖς πάλαι πρεπόντως γινόμενον, ἀποστολικῷ μάλιστα κρατυνθὲν ἐγχειρήματι, τὸ ὅπως ἔχομεν περὶ πίστεως γράφομεν. Καὶ τοῖς θεοσόφοις ὑμῖν πρὸς δοκιμὴν ἀποστέλλομεν, ἵνα μὴ ὅρια μετατιθέντες αἰώνια, ἅπερ ἡμῶν οἱ Πατέρες ἔθεντο δόξωμεν, οὐ διακρίνειν μόνον εἰδόσιν ἀπὸ τῶν νόθων τὰ δοκίμια δόγματα, ἀλλὰ καὶ προσαναπληροῦν τὰ λείποντα διὰ τὴν καὶ ἐν Χριστῷ τελείαν ἀγάπην δυναμένοις ἀκριβῶς καὶ ἰσχύουσιν. Ἐκεῖνα γοῦν λέγειν ἐλεύσομαι, ἅπερ ἀπ' ἀρχῆς ἐν Ἐκκλησίᾳ τῇ ἁγίᾳ καὶ καθολικῇ τεχθεὶς καὶ τραφεὶς ἐκμεμάθηκα, κἀξ ἀπαλῶν φρονεῖν ὀνύχων παρεῖληφα, καὶ κηρυττόντων ὑμῶν τῶν θεοπνεύστων ἀκήκοα.
Πιστεύω τοίνυν, μακάριοι, καθάπερ ἀρχῆθεν πεπίστευκα, εἰς ἕνα Θεὸν Πατέρα παντοκράτορα, ἄναρχον παντελῶς καὶ ἀΐδιον, πάντων ὁρατῶν τε καὶ ἀοράτων Ποιητήν. Καὶ εἰς ἕνα Κύριον Ἰησοῦν Χριστὸν τὸν Υἱὸν τοῦ Θεοῦ τὸν μονογενῆ, τὸν ἀϊδίως καὶ ἀπαθῶς ἐξ αὐτοῦ γεννηθέντα τοῦ Θεοῦ καὶ Πατρός· καὶ οὐκ ἄλλην ἀρχὴν ἢ τὸν Πατέρα γινώσκοντα, ἀλλ' οὐδὲ ἀλλοθέν ποθεν ἢ ἐκ τοῦ Πατρὸς τὴν ὑπόστασιν ἔχοντα· φῶς ἐκ φωτὸς ὁμοούσιον, Θεὸν ἀληθινὸν ἐκ Θεοῦ ἀληθινοῦ συναΐδιον. Εἰς ἓν Πνεῦμα ἅγιον τὸ ἐκ Θεοῦ Πατρὸς ἐκπορευόμενον, τὸ φῶς καὶ Θεὸν καὶ αὐτῷ γνωριζόμενον, καὶ ὃν ἀληθῶς Πατρὶ καὶ Υἱῷ συναΐδιον, ὁμοούσιόν τε καὶ ὁμόφυλον, καὶ τῆς αὐτῆς οὐσίας καὶ φύσεως, καὶ ὡσαύτως δὲ καὶ θεότητος.
Τριάδα ὁμοούσιον καὶ ὁμότιμον καὶ ὁμόθρονον, συμφυῆ καὶ συγγενῆ καὶ ὁμόδοξον, εἰς μίαν συγκεφαλαιουμένην θεότητα, καὶ εἰς μίαν συναγομένην κοινὴν κυριότητα, ἄνευ προσωπικῆς ἀναχύσεως, καὶ ὑποστατικῆς ἐκτὸς συναιρέσεως. Τριάδα γὰρ ἐν μονάδι πιστεύομεν, καὶ μονάδα ἐν Τριάδι δοξάζομεν· Τριάδα μὲν ταῖς τρισὶν ὑποστάσεσι, μονάδα δὲ τῷ μοναδικῷ τῆς θεότητος. Ἥ τε γὰρ ἁγία Τριὰς ἀριθμητή ταῖς προσωπικαῖς ἐστιν ὑποστάσεσιν, ἥ τε παναγία μονὰς πάσης ἐκτός ἐστιν ἀριθμήσεως.
pass_a_gloss: Gloss: 'Serving this custom, we too — holding as finest law that all done fittingly by the ancients, especially what was confirmed by apostolic enterprise, should stand — write the how-we-hold concerning faith. We send [it] to you, the God-taught, for testing, so that we may not seem to be shifting eternal bounds which our fathers set: [you] who know not only to separate the tested dogmas from the bastard ones, but also to fill up the things lacking, through the perfect love in Christ, being able exactly and strong. I shall go on to say the things which, born and reared in the holy and catholic Church, I thoroughly learned from the beginning, and received from tender nails as [my] thinking, and heard from you the God-inspired ones preaching. — I believe then, blessed ones, as I have believed from the start, in one God Father almighty, altogether unoriginate and eternal, Maker of all visible and invisible. And in one Lord Jesus Christ, the Son of God the only-begotten, begotten eternally and impassibly from God himself and Father; knowing no other beginning than the Father, nor having his hypostasis from elsewhere than from the Father; light from light, homoousios, true God from true God, co-eternal. In one Holy Spirit, proceeding from God the Father, known as light and God together with him, truly co-eternal with Father and Son, homoousios and of the same stock, and of the same essence and nature, and likewise also of godhead. — A Trinity homoousios, equal in honour, same-throned, connatural, kindred, same-gloried, recapitulated into one godhead and gathered into one common lordship, without personal pouring-together and apart from hypostatic contraction. For we believe a Trinity in a Monad and glorify a Monad in a Trinity: a Trinity by the three hypostases, a Monad by the singleness of the godhead. For the holy Trinity is countable by its personal hypostases, and the all-holy Monad is outside all counting.' Key lemmas: ἔθος = custom (of synodical letters on accession); δοκιμή = examination/testing; νόθων / δοκίμια = spurious / tested-genuine; ἄναρχον = without beginning; ἀπαθῶς = impassibly; ὁμοούσιος = of one essence; συναΐδιον = co-eternal; ὁμόφυλον = of the same stock/nature; ἀνάχυσις = confusion/pouring together; συναίρεσις = contraction/merging.
pass_b_english:
In keeping with this custom, then, we too observe it, and we hold it the finest of laws that everything done fittingly by those of old should stand — above all, what has been strengthened by apostolic undertaking — and so we write how we stand with regard to the faith. And we send it to you, who are taught of God, for your examination, lest we be thought to be moving the eternal landmarks that our fathers set (Proverbs 22:28): you who know not only how to distinguish the tested doctrines from the spurious, but who can also supply what is lacking, exactly and with strength, because of the perfect love that is in Christ as well. I shall proceed, then, to say the things that I learned thoroughly from the beginning — born and reared in the holy and catholic Church, things I received from tender nails onward as the very way to think, and heard from you, the God-inspired preachers.
I believe, then, blessed ones, just as I have believed from the beginning, in one God, the Father almighty, wholly without beginning and eternal, Maker of all things visible and invisible. And in one Lord Jesus Christ, the only-begotten Son of God, begotten of God the Father himself eternally and without passion, who knows no origin other than the Father and has his subsistence from nowhere else than from the Father: light from light, of one essence, true God from true God, co-eternal. And in one Holy Spirit, who proceeds from God the Father, who is himself known together with him as light and as God, who is in truth co-eternal with the Father and the Son, of one essence and of the same stock, and of the same essence and nature, and likewise also of the same godhead.
A Trinity of one essence, of equal honour, and sharing one throne, of the same nature, of the same kindred, and of the same glory, recapitulated into one godhead and gathered into one common lordship, without confusion of persons and apart from any contracting together of hypostases. For we believe in a Trinity within a Unity, and we glorify a Unity within a Trinity: a Trinity in its three hypostases, a Unity in the singleness of the godhead. For the holy Trinity is countable in its personal hypostases, while the all-holy Unity stands outside all counting.

lemmas.gloss: custom/practice — here the custom of a newly enthroned patriarch sending a synodical letter of faith

lemmas.form: ἀπὸ τῶν νόθων τὰ δοκίμια δόγματα
lemmas.gloss: tested and genuine / spurious, bastard — the contrast is genuine coinage vs counterfeit
idiom: 'from tender nails' = from earliest childhood
of one and the same essence
proceeds (of the Spirit, from the Father; cf. John 15:26)
contraction, drawing together into one (of hypostases)

choices.english: the custom of sending a synodical confession of faith on accession (explained in the translator notes of the book, kept as 'this custom' in the text)
choices.why: The Greek assumes the reader knows the custom; the reading text keeps Sophronius' word and the note carries the explanation, rather than importing words into his sentence.
rejected: expanding the text to 'the custom of synodical letters'

choices.why: Creedal phrase (Nicaea); kept in its familiar English form, matching the Greek exactly.
φυλή/φῦλον is kindred stock; 'of the same nature' would collapse it into the following οὐσίας καὶ φύσεως and lose the distinct word.
συγκεφαλαιοῦσθαι is the Pauline 'sum up under one head' (cf. Ephesians 1:10); 'recapitulated' preserves the deliberate echo.
rejected: 'summed up into one godhead' in Pass B (kept in the gloss register of Pass A)
